observations: body L2-L3: the dashes of «al–kawkab» and «as–samā’» measure 5.4 and 5.5 pt, long dashes. A spot stands over the u of «Caelum» and over the a of «ab»; they are not signs.
body L6: the heavy bracket opens Schiaparelli's addition, which continues on the next page.

body L9-L17: the figure stands at the left of lines 9 to 17, which are set beside it in a narrow measure. It is redrawn from measurements of the print: the sphere as an arc of a circle from the lower end of the ecliptic over the top to Z, drawn whole where it printed with a small break at the upper right; the equator and the ecliptic as straight lines through the first point of Aries; the circle of latitude QAHC and the circles of declination PAKB and PHI as arcs; the bold italic letters, the sign of Aries and the italic words aequator and ecliptica.

body L18-L28: the derivation is checked. In the triangle AHP, sin APH : sin AH = sin PAH : sin PH, where PAH is the supplement of PAQ and PH = 90° − D; in the triangle AQP, sin PAQ : sin QP = sin PQA : sin PA, where PQA is measured by HX = 90° − L and PA = 90° − δ; together they give (α), which differs from L7 by cos D in place of R.
body L20, L21, L38: the minus signs are printed as long dashes (9.6 to 10.6 pt); they are set as minus signs.
body L26: Nallino's addenda et emendanda (Part I, p. LXXIII) read «194,26, lineola excidit in fractione cos L / cos δ.»; the fraction bar, which did not print, is set.
body L35: the dashes of «21–22» and «al–Battānī» are long dashes (5.4 pt).
body L38: Delambre's sign of right ascension is printed as a ligature of italic A and R; it is set as A and R joined.

body L36-L41: Delambre's formulas are checked: in the triangle ABC, right-angled at B, cos AC = cos AB cos CB and tg CB = tg AC cos C, and with cos C = sin ε cos L, AC = β + β′ and AB = δ, sin CB = sin (β + β′) sin ε cos L / cos δ.
body L40: Nallino's addenda et emendanda (Part I, p. LXXIII) read «194, in paenultima formula pro “sin ω” l. “sin ε”.»; the printed «sin ω» is kept (Delambre's ω is ε, L36).
